title: TMotorCANControl physical motor torque, ADC and servo bench logs
authors: University of Michigan Neurobionics Lab (repository owner)
g1_scope: R2 actuator input, closed-loop response and identification
evidence: Public files downloaded, schema and generating or consuming code inspected, numeric outputs recomputed.

queries.retention: Inspect experimental data, canonical producer and reader; avoid software-only, synthetic-only and video-only entries.

neighboring_searches: GitHub README queries: "series elastic actuator" data; "actuator" "dynamometer" robot; exoskeleton actuator test data; "torque tracking" actuator.

DataCite datasets, up to 100/query: "series elastic actuators"; "torque tracking"; "torque control" AND exoskeleton; "quasi-direct drive"; "actuator characterization"; titles.title:(actuator AND torque).
aliases: AK80-9 torque model and Futek load measurements
rights: Public repository. Package metadata specifies GPLv3 and root LISCENSE contains GPL v3. No separate experimental-data license identified in the analyzed directories. Link raw files at fixed revision; include independently computed summary facts and original analysis only.

history.normalization: NFKD, Unicode alphanumeric casefold across text, decompressed gzip and tar member contents; matched all literal normalized aliases.

method: Separate output-torque commands and internal torque/current/speed estimates from torque read by the external ADC. The servo files name the Futek torque and measured ADC voltage, whereas the six-field MIT files name the ADC torque. Preserve original sign for file bounds. Only within sys_ID_final apply the minus-ADC sign in the source trial8 model.

Parse fixed first six fields with csv.reader. Three physical files have a seventh zero-valued column on 7,800 rows despite six names. The pinned trial9 writer appends _times_past_current_limit as its seventh element; the same meaning cannot be established separately for every historical writer.

For fitting, omit the first data row as in the released reader; reproduce its five features using gr=9, kt=0.091, epsilon=0.1 and OLS via numpy.linalg.lstsq. Fix trial8 training data in advance and test each other sys_ID_final CSV; compare predicted torque, internal estimate and logged command to the external ADC. Absolute signed mean residuals below 1e-12 Nm displayed as 0. Classify covariate exceedances by the observed maxima of trial8.

Plateau table includes exact repeated commands for at least five samples; evaluate the final ceil(n/4) samples without filtering or fitting. Record median and 10th/90th quantiles of sign-adjusted ADC. These are repeated logged reference values.

For servo data verify the published 40 Nm/V affine loadcell scaling using ADC voltage minus Futek torque/40 and per-file tare span; the source collects 500 tare samples. Compare desired vs observed speed only for logs with a named desired velocity. Canonical SHA-256 joins parsed header/cells with unit separators and LF for comparison across CSV line endings; retain raw file hashes separately.
findings: 72 distinct torque CSVs, 404,336 rows. In trial8, the released formula labelled RMSE computes sqrt(mean(error)^2); evaluating exactly that statistic gives numerically zero while true sqrt(mean(error^2)) is 1.73097486 Nm on 3,299 fitted samples.

6 other files evaluated with frozen trial8 coefficients. True RMSE for trial5, trial6 and trial9-compensation is 0.818957, 1.001072 and 1.263726 Nm. Early trial1–3 range/external-check failures are 43.1843, 175.140 and 38.2193 Nm; in each some predictor magnitudes exceed the training range.

In trial1–3 final repeated-label tails, the median external torque lies within 0.054 Nm of zero even though absolute logged command is about 25 Nm. The ramp writer explains why a plateau in this column is insufficient evidence of an applied 25 Nm command.

52 servo paths yield 35 distinct parsed tables, 3,437 unique-content rows, 20 tables with explicit desired velocity (1,947 rows). 17 archived paths repeat identical cells. The largest within-file implied tare span is under 9e-16 V. In one 30-row log the desired speed is 10 rad/s while speed, duty and iq are zero throughout; this documents a command–response discrepancy with unknown cause.
bounds: A package status or controller torque estimate is not an independent output torque sensor. Motor serial numbers, calibration certificate, raw ADC device time, power rails, actual post-limit torque command and comparable test fixtures are not confirmed for every legacy trial.

The ramp writer logs its last nonzero Python torque variable before each output update, then commands zero after ten seconds. trial1–3 show matching repeated ±25 Nm labels after ramp end. Their near-zero late external torque must not be interpreted as sustained 25 Nm command or physical saturation without a transmitted-command trace. The dated logger snapshot is evidence of a plausible concrete mechanism, not a proven byte-identical historical acquisition program.

The 6 cross-file comparisons are retrospective, not an original author-defined external holdout, and may differ in firmware/scaling, load or orientation. Huge earlier errors and extreme motor readbacks must not be pooled with later-range tests as nominal performance. Duty units and plateau cause are not inferred. Servo and MIT groups are separate acquisitions, never row-joined.
raw_inputs: All CSVs under src/TMotorCANControl/test/saved_logs with the six named command/ADC/controller fields and all CSVs under src/TMotorCANControl/test/servo_can with a named Futek Torque (Nm) field.

steps: Create a temporary checkout: git clone --no-checkout https://github.com/neurobionics/TMotorCANControl.git checkout
Compare CSV SHA-256 to derived_files. No robot hardware, ROS or source training environment required.
